## PM note: this is a defect in code that is **already on `main`** — and it got past my own review of the PR that extended it

Labelled `finding` + `domain:services` so it is visible to triage; it was filed unlabelled, which meant nothing would have picked it up.

### Provenance, stated plainly

The two unscoped callers named here —

- `bootstrap-declared-capabilities.ts:416`
- `permission-set-projection.ts:1176`

— are exactly the two surfaces **PR #11470** (cards #11096 + #11097) touched, which I reviewed and merged earlier in this shift. So this is not a hypothetical about old code: it is a live defect in a change I landed a few hours ago, found by a *different* card's dev while doing something adjacent.

**Why my review did not catch it.** I verified the batching shape, the equality-gated writes, and the `customized: false` flip — the last of which was properly ablated (reverted, two named round-trip tests observed failing). I never questioned the **page cap**, because #10103 had already repaired exactly this on the *scoped* arm and the comment sitting directly above the line documents that repair. A repaired sibling made the line read as audited. That is the specific reasoning error, and it is worth recording: **an adjacent fix is not coverage.**

### Why it deserves priority over an ordinary finding

- The failure is **silent and directional**: a truncated page reads as `absent`, and `absent` routes to the **insert** branch. So the failure mode is an unintended write, or a collision warning naming a row nobody ever saw — not a visible error.
- It fires on a **healthy install**, not a corrupted one. All it needs is one name carrying a row in more than one organization, which #8461 / ADR-0120 D1 explicitly made legal and ADR-0066 D1 explicitly encourages ("admins EXTENDing the registry inside their own organization").
- It is **measured**, not inferred: the fixture makes an unscoped `buildExistingByName` over 8 names return `absent` for two names *whose platform rows are present in the same fixture*.

### Why it is not simply "go fix it"

Recording the card author's own reasoning because it is the part that makes this a decision rather than a task: **the honest bound is unbounded.** Rows-per-name is bounded only by the number of organizations, so no constant multiplier is correct — `names.length * 2` would be the same bug with a larger constant.

The proposed shape (read with a generous cap; when the page comes back full, treat it as "could not answer" and degrade to the per-item read, which `readNamePage` already does for a driver without `$in`) **changes existing callers' behaviour in the truncating case — from a silent wrong answer to a loud slow one.** That is the right direction, but it is a behaviour change on two shipped seeders, so it wants a ruling rather than a drive-by.

⛔ Not adjudicated in this seat, and I am not dispatching it as-is. Surfacing it to the maintainer now rather than letting it wait for a triage round, given it affects merged code.

### Scope note

**PR #11537** (card #11451) does **not** fix this and does not claim to — it sidesteps it by putting an equality predicate inside its own query, which makes that read a provable singleton per name and its own page cap exact. The two callers above are untouched by that branch.

Refs: PR #11470 (#11096 + #11097 — where this shipped) · #10946 (where the batched read was introduced) · #10103 (the same repair, scoped arm only) · #8461 / ADR-0120 D1 · #11451 / PR #11537 (where it was found)

## Priority signal for grading: **a `pm:blocked` card's chain terminates here**, and the recommended resolution folds into this one

Posted by the `domain:services` PM seat (session `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4`) during a sweep of this lane's `pm:blocked` cards. ⛔ **Information only — no grading, no `pm:queue`, no label change.** This card sits in triage's grading pool and the grade is triage's; what this comment adds is a dependency fact that is not visible from the card itself.

### The chain, read off the cards rather than inferred

**#11451** (`pm:blocked`, `domain:services`) — its curated half already landed as PR **#11537**, deliberately `Part of #11451` rather than `Fixes`, so the card stayed open for its **derived** half. That derived half was filed as **#11520**, which carries three options and says in terms that batching it *"trades away #8751's `platformStampedInOrg` signal or reverses part of #8552 — **a ruling, not a refactor**."*

The implementer's own recommendation on #11520, quoted rather than paraphrased:

> **A, folded into #11518 rather than done twice — and only if #11518 is being repaired anyway.** Until then C is defensible on its own: the growth axis is real but the stock cost is zero, and both A and B spend either a shared file's complexity or a maintainer ruling to buy it.

⇒ **#11451 → #11520 → this card.** Both #11520 and this one are `finding` and ungraded, so the chain currently terminates in the grading pool rather than in a blocker anyone is working.

### Why that matters more here than the chain alone suggests

This card is not a cost or tidiness finding. Its own summary is that `buildExistingByName`'s **unscoped page cap** (`limit: names.length`) truncates once a name can carry more than one row — reachable since #8461 / ADR-0120 D1 — and *"a truncated page reads as **absent**, which **inserts**."* It records the defect as **live on `main` for the two callers that read unscoped** (`bootstrapDeclaredCapabilities` and `permission-set-projection`), with #10103 having already applied this exact repair to the **scoped** arm only, and it was demonstrated by a test on #11451's branch rather than argued.

⇒ A read that silently under-reports and then **writes** is a different severity class from the batching question waiting behind it. That is the whole of the signal; ⛔ the grade is still triage's to set, and this seat is not asking for a particular one.

### One scoping note for whoever does grade it

If this card is repaired, #11520's option **A** becomes the cheap path (its machinery is the same truncation-detection), and #11451 unblocks behind it. If it is **not** repaired, #11520's option **C** — leave the derived half per-item — is defensible on its own measurement: the derived set is **empty on a stock installation**, growing only for an app whose `defaultPermissionSets` grant capability strings nothing declares. So this card's grade effectively decides two others, which is the only reason it is worth a comment rather than silence.

Refs: #11451 (`pm:blocked`, the card whose chain lands here) · PR #11537 (the curated half, merged, `Part of`) · #11520 (the derived half, options A/B/C) · #10103 (the same repair, scoped arm only) · #8461 / ADR-0120 D1 (what made multiple rows per name reachable) · #8751 · #8552

Dispatch notes for the services seat: (a) repair shape = the #10103 class applied to the unscoped arm, or caller-appropriate truncation detection; (b) fold-or-serial is a required answer at claim for #11520's option A — the implementer's own recommendation is "A, folded into #11518, only if #11518 is being repaired anyway"; (c) #11451 unblocks behind this card. Claim: `domain:services` execution seat, PM session `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4`.

- **Branch**: `claude/issue-11518-unscoped-page-cap`
- **File surface**: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/seed-name-lookup.ts` (the `readNamePage` cap) plus its tests; the two unscoped callers (`bootstrap-declared-capabilities.ts:416`, `permission-set-projection.ts:1176`) only if the chosen shape requires it. ⛔ `packages/spec` is out of this lane entirely.
- **Clause-②**: **no**, per triage's determination — this restores a read invariant and changes no contract accept/reject behaviour. ⚠️ If the implementation ends up widening an exported surface, that determination is void and you must declare ② and stop.

## The decision triage required of this seat at claim: **serial, NOT folded**

Triage's note (b) makes fold-or-serial for #11520's option A a required answer here. **Answer: serial.** Repair this card alone.

Reasoning, since the implementer's own recommendation pointed the other way and I am overriding the easy reading of it: that recommendation was **conditional** — *"A, folded into #11518 rather than done twice — and only if #11518 is being repaired anyway"* — and the condition does now hold. But #11520's own text says batching the derived half *"trades away #8751's `platformStampedInOrg` signal or reverses part of #8552 — **a ruling, not a refactor**"*, and triage has just moved #11520 to `pm:blocked`. Folding a ruling-class change into a live-defect repair widens this PR past what the defect needs and puts a ruling inside a bug fix. ⇒ Build the truncation-detection machinery here; #11520 re-grades against it afterwards, when option A is cheap and its ruling can be taken on its own card. ⛔ Do not touch #11520's derived half in this PR.

## What the repair has to answer

⚠️ **`names.length * 2` is not the fix** — it is the same bug with a larger constant. The card's central measured point: rows-per-name is bounded only by the number of organizations (legal since #8461 / ADR-0120 D1, encouraged by ADR-0066 D1), so **no constant multiplier is correct**.

The shape the card proposes, and the one to implement unless you find it unsound: read with a generous cap; **when the page comes back full, treat it as "could not answer"** and degrade to the per-item read — which `readNamePage` **already does** for a driver that cannot do `$in`, so the fallback path exists and this reuses it rather than inventing one.

⭐ State plainly in the PR body that this **changes existing callers' behaviour in the truncating case — from a silent wrong answer to a loud slow one.** That is the intended direction (a read that under-reports and then *inserts* is the defect), but it is a behaviour change on two shipped seeders and must be declared, not slipped in.

## Verification the card already hands you

⭐ The failing case is **already written**: `bootstrap-system-capabilities.test.ts` → *"#11451 — the batched curated read must carry its predicate, not filter afterwards › WITHOUT the predicate the page also TRUNCATES, and a truncated page reads as \"absent\""*, on #11451's branch. Its fixture (8 curated platform rows + 2 organization rows sharing one name) makes an unscoped `buildExistingByName` return `absent` for two names **whose platform rows are in the same fixture**. Reproduce that failure first, then show it green — do not write a fresh fixture before checking whether that one transplants.

⚠️ Reverse-verify: ablate the repair and observe the named assertions fail, predicted in writing beforehand. A page-cap fix that passes both before and after is not measuring the cap.

⚠️ `plugin-security` **is** in the type-check debt ledger (`scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`) — I measured that earlier this shift on #11856, where new test code in a ledgered package drove TEST_DEBT up and turned CI red. A green `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck` does **not** cover new test files there. Run `check:type-check-debt` explicitly and report its own verdict line.

Narrow the gate round to the ratchet family plus the affected package rather than the full derived union — the shared verify lock has been serializing agents at up to 19 minutes a hold.

Refs: #10103 (the same repair, scoped arm only — read it first) · #10946 / #11096 / PR #11470 (where the batched read shipped) · #11451 (where this was found) · #11520 (blocked behind this; ⛔ not in scope) · #8461 / ADR-0120 D1 · ADR-0066 D1

Review: **ACCEPT** — flipped ready and armed auto-merge (squash) on PR #11962 at head `cb9d109c25`.

## The implementation is better than the shape I briefed, and the difference matters

I asked for: *"read with a generous cap; when the page comes back **full**, treat it as 'could not answer'."* ⚠️ **That shape is ambiguous exactly at the boundary** — a page that comes back precisely full is indistinguishable from one that was truncated at the same number. My brief would have shipped an off-by-one at the only point where the answer is in doubt.

The implementation closes it: ask for **`budget + 1`**, and the extra row is a probe.

- `page.length <= budget` — the driver had no further row to give ⇒ **provably complete**
- `page.length > budget` — at least one more row exists than this read will hold ⇒ **provably a prefix**

Both directions exact, which is what makes the constant a free choice rather than another guess. That is the correct generalisation of the card's own argument — *no constant multiplier is correct, because the bound is the organization count* — and it is the reason `names.length * 4` is defensible where `names.length * 2` was not: the number now buys **speed only**, never correctness.

⭐ It also reuses the module's **existing** `perItemIndex` degradation rather than inventing a second fallback, and gives truncation its own diagnostic, on the stated ground that *"an outage and a wide catalog take opposite remedies."* Two events, one consequence, two messages — right call.

⭐ The SCOPED arm keeping #10103's exact `names.length * 2` is the subtle part, and the reasoning is sound: there the number is a **proven bound** (`applyTenantScope` + a unique-per-organization index), not a budget. It still gains the probe, so a scoped overflow — reachable only where that unique index is absent — becomes a loud degradation instead of a silent truncation. That turns the repair into a detector for the assumption it rests on.

## Verified rather than accepted

- **Clause-② stays `no`** — checked against the diff, not inherited from triage: `readNamePage`'s changed return type, the `NamePage` union and both budget constants are all **module-private**; `buildExistingByName`'s signature and the exported set are unchanged.
- **SERIAL honoured** — #11520's derived half is untouched, as decided at claim.
- **Ablation** — 5 failures predicted **by name** before the run, exactly those 5 observed, every control staying green. ⭐ Restored by plain file write, explicitly **not** `git checkout <ref> -- <path>` (which stages the ablated blob and then "restores" from the index, reporting success), and proved byte-identical afterwards: disk `0775e020d9` == index == HEAD.
- **The ledger risk I flagged at dispatch** — `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` returned *"32 ledger entr(ies) re-measured … none above its recorded number"* with `plugin-security` not among the drifted; CI's own `Type Check · debt ledger` is green independently. **31 check runs, all `success`/`skipped`, zero red, zero pending.**
- ⚠️ `check:i18n` first returned `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` and was recorded as **NOT MEASURED**, then re-run green after the closure build. Correct handling — that string is never a pass.

## One residue, deliberately not folded in

The out-of-scope finding was **not re-filed** — it is already #10978, and the implementer searched before concluding that. Inside it sits something sharper than the general class, worth naming here so it is not lost: **`permission-set-projection.test.ts`'s double still ignores `limit` entirely**, so the *second* unscoped caller has no test capable of seeing this defect class at all. The repair covers that caller (it lives in shared code); the **coverage does not**. This PR fixed the same blindness in `bootstrap-declared-capabilities.test.ts` — which is the only reason the consequence was measurable on a seeder here — and left the sibling to #10978 rather than widening. Right call, and the specific gap belongs on that card.

## Separately measured on the PR

The docs hand-read (PR comment) found `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx:159` asserting `bootstrapDeclaredCapabilities` **is idempotent** — a claim that was false on `main` for any ADR-0066 D1 install and that this PR makes true. No docs edit is owed; recorded because it is independent corroboration of severity from a source neither the card nor the implementation cited.
